cards.note: The 67C is a mountain road with all yellow road lines.
The 7C is recognisable as going through some of the most dramatic mountains in Romania, with very green and lush vegetation. It also has distinct long and spiraling roads.

In the city of Baia Mare those distinct red with white outline house numbers are common.

**Note: **They were introduced in 2024 so won't be found in earlier copyrights.

In the city of Baia Mare those distinct red with white outline street signs are common. They can be in the surrounding towns as well, thought usually the red will be replaced by another color.

**Note: **They were introduced in 2024 so won't be found in earlier copyrights.
Bilingual signs with Hungarian are mostly found in the central regions of Covasna, Harghita and Mureş, but also less commonly near the Hungarian border.

Street signs in Bucharest will often have written "sector" on them which means "district" and can be found within the city. Sometimes the sign can look very similar to the Paris street sign: big, blue and with a green outline.
Street signs in Buzău will often have this logo on them resembling the letter B.
The city of Cluj has those vertical white stickers of 3 numbers and a letter.
Street signs in Constanța will often be white with a black,thin border but will also have this distinct logo on them.
In north-east Romania the yellow stickers on the poles are usually very long. The name of the town/village can often be found in the middle of the sticker.
Elaborately decorated wooden gates can be found in Maramureș, in the North-West

In the eastern half of Romania, it is very common to have plastic fake tiled or metal roofs. As well as the roofs seem to have more diverse colors. If most roofs you see are metal or plastic fake tiled, you are likely in the eastern half. In the center there is a combination of different roof types

In north-west Romania you can find those red electricity warning which are on a white background. In the rest of the country the background is mostly yellow. The North-West region can also have yellow background on the warning sign

Note: You can find similar sticks in other regions but it's by far the most common in the north-west

In the western half of Romania, it is very common to have orange tiled roofs. If most roofs you see are orange tiled, you are likely in the western half. In the center there is a combination of different roof types

Orange vertical pole stickers with numbers on them can be found in Bucharest, Galati, Iasi, Piatra Neamt, Baia Mare and Craiova.

Note: In Iasi the sticker is 6 digits long, in the other cities it is usually 5 digits long.
The city of Sibiu often has those windows at roof level which look like a squinting eye.

In south-center Romania there are often stickers on poles that can give the region away.

Besides the well known rectangle stickers, within the south of Romania there are also those brown E stickers and also green D stickers.

Note: The stickers can be used interchangeably, if you see any one of those stickers then it is that region.
In south-center Romania there are often small green rectangles. If they can be read, the first 2 letters are abbreviation of the county you are in.
Within Timisoara a lot of the poles have those vertical stickers with 5 numbers and a QR code at the top.

In Transylvania it's not uncommon to see crosses on top of the roof, the darker areas are where there is a very high concentration of roof crosses and the lighter areas it's still common but you might have to move a bit to find them. This meta can slightly "bleed" into the neighboring counties around the border. In Maramures county a variant of the cross can be found with an arch above it!

Note: It is extremely rare to find crosses on roofs outside of those areas, so rare that I'm not sure they exist since I didn't find any.

Fairly often you'll see those big signs which usually are blue or white and can tell you exactly where you are.

Some useful words

  • Județ(abbreviated as jud.) - County (can be read while zooming in the dotted lines)
  • Municipiul - City
  • Localitate - City
  • Comună/Sat - Village

Often on the side of the road KM markers can be found in different colors (red, blue, yellow, white) and the color should also represent the color the road will show up on the map. On the side is the road number and usually on the front are two cities, the first one is the closest largest city and the second one is the closest town.
Wind turbine farms can be found in the very east of Romania in the counties of Constanța and Tulcea, as well as in the west.
